thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: synth-probe-prod-eu/l7-health triggered 3 failures in 8m (latency > 1200ms). Paging current oncall @Jordan H..
Jordan H.: I'm on it — looking at the synthetic probe trace now. Opening the EU inference dashboard.
Jordan H.: quick glance: spikes around 12:02 and 12:09, short-lived. No obvious backend 5xx in logs, just higher tail latency on a subset of hosts.
Alex P.: saw similar earlier this week — could be noisy VM flapping or a bad kernel update on a small pool. Any host-level alerts?
Sam R.: checking host metrics now, tail CPU and steal look normal. Disk io fine. Network egress for the region shows a tiny blip at 12:02 (0.3% of interfaces).
Maria G.: can we confirm if this affected customer traffic, or was it isolated to the probe path?
Jordan H.: looked at production request traces: no customer errors, a handful of requests had +300ms extra latency but still under SLO. So customer impact = minimal.
Jordan H.: root message timestamp: 1968004321
Alex P.: the probe config currently:
```yaml
probe:
  name: synth-probe-prod-eu
  interval_seconds: 60
  timeout_seconds: 10
  consecutive_failures: 3
  latency_threshold_ms: 1200
  check_type: l7-health
```
Alex P.: with interval 60s and consecutive_failures=3, a single spike every ~2m will trigger a page. That's likely our noise source.
Sam R.: suggestion: debounce using consecutive_failures=5 and increase interval to 120s for this probe while we investigate. Also add a rolling-median filter (5m) in alert rule.
Maria G.: +1. Also add a short suppression window (5m) after a probe is auto-recovered to avoid repeats during flappy maintenance windows.
Jordan H.: I'm going to mute paging for this probe and create a backend-only alert that logs to the incidents channel for a day while we tune thresholds. Will annotate the alert with 'tuning-in-progress'.
Ops Desk: note created: Jira INFR-4321 - "Canary: tuning prod-eu probe to reduce false positives". Assigned to Jordan H.
Jordan H.: Proposed new probe config I will push to staging:
```yaml
probe:
  name: synth-probe-prod-eu
  interval_seconds: 120
  timeout_seconds: 12
  consecutive_failures: 5
  latency_threshold_ms: 1600
  filters:
    - rolling_median_minutes: 5
    - ignore_1xx_2xx_spikes: true
  suppression_minutes_after_recovery: 5
```
Alex P.: bumping the latency threshold to 1600ms seems safe given customer traces. Also add region-aware thresholds in case EU spikiness is normal at times of infra jobs.
Maria G.: also recommend adding a health-tag to indicate whether the probe path uses dedicated cache warmers — those can cause transient latency if cache misses spike.
Sam R.: I'll create a quick Grafana panel showing per-host p50/p95/p99 for the probe path and add an annotation stream for probe triggers so we can correlate.
Jordan H.: updating runbook: under 'Synthetic probe noisy alarms' we'll add steps:
1) Check customer impact (traces + SLOs)
2) Look for host/network flaps in last 15m
3) If no customer impact and short-lived: mute paging, create tuning ticket, switch probe to non-paging mode, increase consecutive_failures and interval, add rolling filter
4) If customer impact: escalate to infra + model-oncall, roll back recent infra changes if correlated
Jordan H.: pushing config change to staging now, will run 2h of non-paging logging to validate.
Alex P.: reminder: update alert rule in Prometheus/Alertmanager to something like:
```yaml
expr: increase(synthetic_probe_failures_total{probe="prod-eu"}[10m]) >= 5
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://company.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-4321
```
Maria G.: please also add a dashboard widget for 'probe noise rate' (failures / checks) with a 1h moving avg, that'll help spot regressions after tuning.
Sam R.: agreed. I'll add the panel and a dedicated alert that doesn't page but posts to #incidents if 1h moving avg > 0.02 (2%).
Jordan H.: 1h validation complete in staging with the new config — we had 2 probe triggers but none would have paged. No customer impact observed.
Jordan H.: I'm going to roll the non-paging config to prod at 13:45, annotate the probe in the inventory, and leave paging disabled for 24h while we monitor.
Maria G.: can you also add a short note in the postmortem: why we chose interval 120s, consecutive_failures 5, and latency threshold 1600ms (include sample percentiles)?
Jordan H.: will do. Draft postmortem summary: "Brief probe noise caused pages to oncall due to 60s interval + low consecutive_failures. No customer impact. Tuned probe to reduce sensitivity (interval 120s, consecutive_failures 5, rolling median 5m). Added dashboards and non-paging logging for 24h. Follow-up: consider per-region baseline thresholds and auto-suppress during infra maintenance windows."
Ops Desk: follow-up tasks created: INFR-4322 (dashboard panel + alert), INFR-4323 (runbook update), INFR-4324 (postmortem).
Sam R.: handing off monitoring to Maria for the next 12h. I'll keep an eye on the annotation stream.
Jordan H.: handing over to Maria G. for daytime coverage — contact details in the Jira. If the probe starts showing sustained failures (> 10m) re-enable paging immediately.
Maria G.: ack, taking over. I'll do a readout at 4pm and decide whether to restore original sensitivity.
Jordan H.: final note: changed alert labels to include 'probe_owner:eng-oncall' and 'tuning_ticket:INFR-4321' so any future responders see context immediately.
Alex P.: thanks everyone. This looks like a good pattern for noisy synth probes that are low customer-impact.
Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: probe config changed and paging suppressed for 24h (annotated by Jordan H.).
